title: Bakuman。
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Two middle schoolers, an artist and a writer, team up to become professional manga creators and win serialization in Weekly Shonen Jump. The story follows their rivals, editors, cancellations and hits, alongside the artist's long-distance promise to marry a girl who wants to become a voice actress.
life_message: A good life is chasing a dream with a trusted partner through hard, honest work.

content.note: Career setbacks and a relative's death from overwork.
Chaste romance built on a promise to marry; critics called the portrayal of women sexist (Wikipedia; SLJ).
Mild; not flagged by SLJ (rated T, 13+) (to verify).
Overwork leads to hospitalization; the hero's uncle died from overwork (Wikipedia).
Teens push their health for deadlines.
A love letter to the real manga industry, naming real magazines and editors (Wikipedia).

delivery.evidence: Thompson (ANN) says characters state gender views outright and the series praises old-fashioned attitudes; calls female characters grudge-driven viragos or helpmates.
delivery.note: A reviewer finds its views on work and gender stated outright, while noting its villains are among its most interesting characters.

winners_losers: Hard-working creators and their editors win; shortcuts and arrogance lose. A meritocratic, work-ethic worldview gets the sympathy.
